card.name: Ampersand inside publisher and company names
card.fires_on: The linking word or symbol in the middle of a publisher or company name, mostly '&' or 'and' after a first name such as John Wiley, Merck or Allen. It fires just before the next part of the name, such as Sons, Co. or Unwin.

modes.label: Publisher names
modes.description: The '&' or a partial name inside a book publisher's name in a reference list.
modes.example: J.W. Steed and P.A. Gale (eds). John Wiley<< &>> Sons Ltd, Chichester, UK

modes.label: Company names
modes.description: The '&' or 'and' joining parts of a drug or device company name.
modes.example: is a trademark of Becton Dickinson<< and>> Company. Important Administration Information

modes.label: Other institution names
modes.description: A middle word or part of an organisation or press name before its final part.

card.writes: It promotes proper-name continuations and suppresses company-style words like Continental, Pacific and Century.
card.plain: It marks the point in a publisher or company name where an '&' or 'and' comes before the rest of the name.
